title: Two Switches, One Light Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav switches on the stair light at the bottom of the stairs, then switches it off from the top with a different switch. How can two switches share one light? In this animated lesson we meet switches, relays and connectors, the practical parts that make and break real circuits.

First we see a switch as a tap for current and learn poles and throws: SPST, SPDT, DPST and DPDT. On a live breadboard two SPDT switches run a stair light while the truth table fills row by row and an oscilloscope shows the lamp voltage jumping between 0 and 5 V. Then we open a relay: a coil becomes an electromagnet, pulls the armature and moves the common contact from normally closed to normally open, so a small coil current switches a big pump current. We also see why connectors are used (pin headers, screw terminals, plugs and sockets) and the ratings printed on every part. A worked example checks a relay coil current, coil power and whether the contacts can switch a heater, followed by the exam trap (what normally open really means), where it is asked, an original board pattern practice question with a full solution, and a fact card to screenshot.

This is Episode 58 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 9: Practical Electronic Components, their Specifications and PCB (Karnataka I PUC Electronics).
